title: Governor of Maryland

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Wes Moore is seeking a second term; Maryland governors may serve two consecutive terms.
Moore won the Democratic primary with 88.3% over physician Eric Felber.
Former Del. Dan Cox, the 2022 Republican nominee, won a nine-candidate Republican primary, finishing ahead of businessman Ed Hale.
Two minor-party tickets are also on the ballot: Andy Ellis (Green) and Cathy White (Working Class Party). The State Board of Elections ballot lists exactly these four tickets.

candidates.name: Wes Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Running with incumbent Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller. Won the Democratic primary with 88.3%.

summary.text: Wes Moore is the incumbent Governor of Maryland, seeking a second term with Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller. A Rhodes Scholar and Army veteran who served in Afghanistan, he led the Robin Hood Foundation before being elected governor in 2022. In office he has signed measures on housing, immigration enforcement, abortion rights and public safety.

background.text: Graduated from Johns Hopkins University and received a master's degree from Wolfson College, Oxford, as a Rhodes Scholar.
Served in the U.S. Army, including with the 82nd Airborne Division in Afghanistan; later worked as an investment banker.
Served as CEO of the Robin Hood Foundation, a New York anti-poverty organization, before running for governor.

priorities.text: Expanding 'pathways to work, wages, and wealth' for Maryland families.
Housing supply and affordability, including signing the Maryland Housing Certainty Act in 2026.
Public safety, which he said in 2024 the administration had made its “number one priority.”
priorities.quote: When we entered office, we made public safety our number one priority, and we said we were going to move differently on this issue—because the status quo wasn't working.

positions.summary: Signed a proclamation enshrining the right to reproductive freedom in the state constitution after voters approved the amendment in 2024.
positions.quote: Since day one of my administration, I have made clear my support for a woman's right to choose.

positions.summary: Signed SB 245/HB 444 in 2026 prohibiting State and local jurisdictions from entering 287(g) agreements deputizing officers for federal civil immigration enforcement.
Signed the Maryland Housing Certainty Act and the Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act in 2026, which he described as central to his housing priorities.

record.text: Signed SB 245/HB 444, prohibiting Maryland State and local jurisdictions from deputizing officers for federal civil immigration enforcement (287(g) agreements).
Signed more than 274 bills at the final 2026 bill signing, including the Maryland Housing Certainty Act (HB 548/SB 325) and the Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act.
Signed HB 2100, placing a constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot that would clarify redistricting standards do not apply to congressional districts.
Signed a proclamation enshrining 'an individual's fundamental right to reproductive freedom' in Maryland's constitution.
Presided over a 2024 bill signing of public safety bills, including measures to support victims, recruit law enforcement and address gun violence.

candidates.name: Dan Cox
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Robert Krop, a gun store owner. Won the Republican primary.

summary.text: Dan Cox is a Frederick County attorney, a former member of the Maryland House of Delegates, and the Republican nominee for governor for the second time; he lost to Wes Moore in 2022. His campaign emphasizes tax and fee reductions, housing affordability and energy costs.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C., and raised in Frederick County; earned a bachelor's degree from University of Maryland Global Campus (2002) and a J.D. from Regent University School of Law (2006).
Served in the Maryland House of Delegates from January 2019 to January 2023, including on the Judiciary Committee.
Won the 2022 Republican nomination for governor and lost the general election to Wes Moore.

priorities.text: Lowering taxes and fees, including reducing property taxes for seniors.
priorities.quote: we must immediately cease taxing our seniors out of their retirement homes through statewide law and executive action to limit, cap, and, where possible, eliminate property taxes.

priorities.text: Housing affordability for first-time buyers and cutting building costs and permitting burdens.
Lowering energy costs through in-state generation, including reopening closed power plants and studying small modular reactors.

positions.summary: Campaign site proposes cutting building costs and permitting burdens along with down-payment assistance and tax credits for first-time buyers.
positions.quote: slashing ridiculous building costs and permitting burdens that send our builders out of state

record.text: As a delegate, introduced a resolution containing articles of impeachment against Gov. Larry Hogan over his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The House Rules and Executive Nominations Committee voted unanimously to reject the Cox impeachment resolution.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website text covers taxes, housing and energy; no direct statements on guns, abortion or immigration were found for 2026, so no positions were entered on those. Official legislature roll-call PDFs for his House votes could not be read in this environment.

candidates.name: Andy Ellis
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Owen Silverman Andrews, a teacher.

summary.text: Andy Ellis is a Baltimore resident, a volunteer leader of the Maryland Green Party for a decade, and a former House of Delegates candidate. His campaign lists priorities including climate and environment emergency declarations, public education funding and reparations.

background.text: Former co-chair of the Maryland Green Party and candidate for the House of Delegates in 2018.

priorities.text: Declare climate, environment, energy, food and water emergencies.
Build out and fully fund the public education system.

candidates.researchNotes: Only high-level priorities were read; no direct statements on the guide's fixed issue statements were found.

candidates.name: Cathy White
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Cathy Permut.

summary.text: Cathy White is the Working Class Party's candidate for governor and says she has worked for 40 years as a factory production worker. The party won 2026 ballot status by submitting over 12,000 signatures.

background.text: Was the party's candidate for lieutenant governor in 2022.

candidates.researchNotes: Statement posted by the party; no direct statements on the guide's fixed issue statements were found.
